newsitem.title: USA: RJ Reynolds hiked cigarette prices.
newsitem.headline: RJ Reynolds hiked cigarette prices.

text.p: RJ Reynolds Tobacco Co said it raised wholesale cigarette prices by $0.04 per pack.
The price increase, effective Friday, reflects "our increased cost of doing business," said RJ Reynolds spokeswoman Maura Ellis.
The tobacco company said wholesale prices increased by $2.00 per 1000 cigarettes on all products except its Century brand. Century's wholesale prices increased $1.60 per 1000 cigarettes, Ellis said.
RJ Reynolds, a unit of RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp, declined further comment on its pricing strategy.

Analysts said RJ Reynolds raised prices about a month sooner than expected. While tobacco companies typically adjust prices in April, RJ Reynolds moved earlier to prevent distributors from stockpiling products before the next price hike, analysts said.
The sooner-than-expected price hike also will give RJ Reynolds a slight revenue boost in the first quarter, instead of the benefit starting in the second quarter.
"Anyone with earnings estimates below the consensus estimate may have to raise their numbers," said Roy Burry, an analyst with Oppenheimer & Co.
On a consensus basis, Wall Street analysts expect RJR Nabisco to earn $0.66 a share in the first quarter, according to First Call, which tracks analysts estimates.
The price increase will not affect earnings estimates for the full year, since most Wall Street analysts factor in annual price increases of about four to five percent.
Industry analysts expect other tobacco companies to quickly follow RJ Reynolds' lead.
"It's a good bet that the others will follow with comparable increases," said Emanuel Goldman, an analyst with PaineWebber.

Philip Morris Cos Inc declined to comment. Officials from Lorilland Tobacco Co, a unit of Loews Corp, and Brown & Williamson Tobacco Co, a unit of B.A.T Industries Plc's, did not return calls seeking comment.
RJR Nabisco gained 3/8 to 37-3/8, while Philip Morris gained 1-7/8 to 137-7/8.
